domain_restrictions: n, k, and l are integers.
k and l satisfy 0 <= k <= n and 0 <= l <= n.
The q-binomial coefficient is only defined by the given product for integers r in the range 0 <= r <= n.
The empty product is interpreted as 1 when r = 0.
The quotient [n choose k]_q divided by [n choose l]_q is considered as a rational function in q.
The hypothesis requires that this rational function actually belongs to the polynomial ring in q, not merely that it is formally written as a quotient.
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every choice of integers n, k, and l with 0 <= k <= n and 0 <= l <= n, if the ratio of the two q-binomial coefficients [n choose k]_q and [n choose l]_q is a polynomial in q, then min(k, n-k) is at least min(l, n-l).
quantifier_order: For all integers n, k, and l, assume 0 <= k <= n and 0 <= l <= n.
For each integer r with 0 <= r <= n, define the q-binomial coefficient using the stated product, with the empty product equal to 1 when r = 0.
Define k0 as the minimum of k and n-k, and define l0 as the minimum of l and n-l.
If the quotient of the two q-binomial coefficients is a polynomial in q, then the conclusion follows.

variables.name: r
variables.role: index used in the definition of the q-binomial coefficient

variables.domain: variable over the rational function and polynomial expressions in q
variables.name: q
variables.role: symbol in the q-binomial coefficient and its ratio

witness_dependencies: No existential witness is present in the statement.
The derived quantities k0 and l0 depend only on n, k, and l.
The polynomiality condition depends on q through the rational function [n choose k]_q divided by [n choose l]_q.

statement_nl: For integers n, k, and l with 0 <= k <= n and 0 <= l <= n, define [n choose r]_q := product_{i=1}^r (1 - q^(n-r+i)) / (1 - q^i) for 0 <= r <= n, with the empty product equal to 1 when r = 0. Let k0 := min(k, n-k) and l0 := min(l, n-l). If the rational function [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q is actually a polynomial in q, then k0 >= l0.
